meta.title: Ondra Developer Companion
meta.description: Developer companionship for Ondra (L9 extension pool, self-developed): it answers one question — her owner is stuck in the middle of something, should she speak, and what should she say? The shell reports four facts (a build failed, tests went green, a long task finished, a commit landed); she first decides whether to speak at all, then picks a tone. Of the five tones, silence is a first-class one: she says nothing during the quiet window after a failure (the person is editing), the only thing allowed once the same error has been bitten for a while is 'put it down for now' rather than 'try again', she speaks only when red turns green and never praises a green that was never red (praise for every test run makes praise worthless), and she stays silent during a meeting, while away, or when presence cannot be read. No numbers at all: not how many failures, not how long it ran, not how many lines changed — the contract has no numeric field whatsoever. She never reads code, diffs, or implementation, because the code belongs to an employer; the only file access in this package is writing its own ledger, and errors are recognised solely by an opaque fingerprint supplied by the shell, never persisted and never logged. Silence has six distinguishable reasons (still red, in a meeting, away, unreadable, just spoke, nothing new) and may not be folded into one 'muted' state. The ledger holds watermarks and counters only, never event details. No UI, no timers, and it never sends anything on its own.
